cases.name: short ones inside a long one

hints: At the busiest instant of the morning, how many meetings are running?
Interval sweep: sort start times and end times separately (or keep a min-heap of end times).
Walk the sorted starts with a pointer into the sorted ends; if a start is at or after the earliest unused end, advance that pointer and reuse the room, otherwise open a new room.

signals: Restates the goal as peak simultaneous meetings
Uses the start/end sweep or a min-heap of end times and explains why rooms are interchangeable
Applies the half-open rule so back-to-back meetings share a room
Gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space
followups: Return which room each meeting gets, not just the count.
Times are whole minutes within one day. Is there an O(n + T) approach?
Can one person attend every meeting? How is that simpler?
